meta.title: Build a Home Lab
meta.eyebrow: Personal project, from the first server to a stable setup
meta.subtitle: Hardware, virtualization, services and backup
meta.description: A project to build a home server with useful services and backup.
meta.tagline:
A server at home, step by step.
Every phase ends with something working.
meta.sidebarNote:
Write down what you changed.
Back up before touching something that works.

labels.doneHint: Only mark this when the deliverable works and is written down.
labels.legendHint: Click a step to see what it involves, the deliverable and the references.

phases.title: Base
phases.summary: Choose the hardware and get the system installed and reachable.

phases.title: Services
phases.summary: Bring up the services you will actually use.

phases.title: Operations
phases.summary: Backup, monitoring and a maintenance routine.

nodes.title: Pick the hardware
nodes.summary: Decide what the server must do before buying or reusing anything.
nodes.challenge: A list of what will be used, the cost and the estimated power draw.
nodes.success: You know how many services fit on the chosen machine.

nodes.title: Install the system
nodes.summary: Install the hypervisor or the base system and keep everything up to date.
nodes.challenge: System installed, updated and reachable over SSH with a key.
nodes.success: You reboot the server and it comes back on its own, reachable.

tasks.title: Download the image and write it to a USB stick
Install and set up the disk
Create the user and the SSH key

nodes.title: Network and access
nodes.summary: A fixed IP, local names and safe remote access.
nodes.challenge: Reach the server by name at home and from outside through the VPN.
nodes.success: No service is exposed to the internet without a reason.

tasks.title: Reserve a fixed IP on the router
Set up the VPN for remote access

nodes.title: Separate network for the lab
nodes.summary: Isolate the lab from the rest of the network with a VLAN.

nodes.title: Containers with Docker
nodes.summary: Run the services in containers described by versioned files.
nodes.challenge: A test service running through Compose, with its data in a volume.
nodes.success: You recreate the container and the data is still there.

nodes.title: Reverse proxy and certificates
nodes.summary: A single entry point with HTTPS for the services.
nodes.challenge: Two services reachable under different names, both over HTTPS.
nodes.success: Adding a new service takes a few minutes.

nodes.title: DNS with ad blocking
nodes.summary: Your own DNS server for the whole house.
nodes.challenge: Every device at home using the lab DNS.
nodes.success: You can see which queries were blocked and allow one.

nodes.title: Media server
nodes.summary: Organize photos, music and video in a service of your own.

nodes.title: 3-2-1 backup
nodes.summary: Three copies, two kinds of media, one off site.
nodes.challenge: An automatic backup running and a restore that was really tested.
nodes.success: You restore a service from scratch using the backup.

tasks.title: List what goes into the backup
Restore a test service
tasks.note: A backup that was never restored does not count.

nodes.title: Monitoring and alerts
nodes.summary: Know that something broke before you notice by using it.
nodes.challenge: A simple dashboard and an alert when the disk goes over 85 percent.
nodes.success: You receive the alert when you simulate a failure.

nodes.title: Document and automate
nodes.summary: Make the setup reproducible for whoever touches it next, including you in six months.
nodes.challenge: A repository with the configuration and a recovery README.
nodes.success: Someone can rebuild the setup by following only the README.

nodes.title: Automation with Ansible
nodes.summary: Describe the server configuration as code.
